status: Research questions and predicted mechanisms, not estimated behavioral effects or claims of novelty
principle: Use a common medicine and applicant, decompose legal mechanisms, and distinguish written rules from operation. The six comparator papers motivate the design; they do not establish which pharmaceutical questions are previously unanswered.

questions.question: How much of a foreign regulatory investment can a medicine carry into another country?
questions.economic_idea: A foreign scientific assessment can be reused, but its useful legal reach may depend on access to underlying information. Recognition and information-sharing institutions can be complements.
questions.test_with_existing_laws: Compare public-report and complete-report cases for the same medicine. Separate the content of the report from applicant consent and reference-authority permission; record the domestic assessment remaining.
questions.additional_outcome_test: Whether those legal differences predict actual pathway uptake or review time requires named applications and route-use records.

questions.question: Are FDA and European approvals substitutes, or does having both unlock an additional route?
questions.economic_idea: Some rules treat two foreign approvals as complementary signals. A firm can face a different return to its second regulatory investment depending on destination-country institutions.
questions.test_with_existing_laws: Compare FDA-only with FDA plus European Commission authorization for the identical medicine and documentation. Distinguish a two-approval route from a separate one-approval route, and shared EU authorization from national recognition.
questions.additional_outcome_test: Whether firms change the order or timing of submissions requires submission dates and a drug–country risk set.

questions.question: Does one approval create a chain of further approvals, or does the chain stop at the original scientific reviewer?
questions.economic_idea: Recognition need not be transitive. A destination may insist that its reference regulator performed its own full review, concentrating the international value of assessment in a small set of original reviewers.
questions.test_with_existing_laws: Code explicit standalone-review and anti-chaining clauses; compare permissible direct connections with indirect chains. Unknown transitivity remains unknown, and regional authorization systems are separate units.
questions.additional_outcome_test: Measure whether the same original assessment actually supported multiple downstream decisions using named route/reference records.

questions.question: Do countries replace scientific assessment while retaining the administrative costs of entry?
questions.economic_idea: Delegating scientific work and reducing local paperwork are separate policy choices. Fixed procedural costs could remain even when much of the assessment is reusable.
questions.test_with_existing_laws: Compare scientific review, local representative, filing, fees, certification, translation and local-evidence conditions for the fixed medicine. Count a procedure only when the source establishes a distinct mandatory external interaction.
questions.additional_outcome_test: Use fee schedules and a standardized applicant/regulator survey to value compliance costs. More paperwork alone does not establish rent extraction or an inefficient safety rule.

questions.question: Can a foreign approval become too old to help—or too new?
questions.economic_idea: Maximum-age rules can make a regulatory shortcut expire, while minimum marketing-history rules reward waiting. Different rules can create opposing entry incentives for the same medicine.
questions.test_with_existing_laws: Keep the medicine constant and vary time since reference approval across6,18,36 and72 months. Separate minimum age, maximum age, safety-history and foreign-marketing conditions, with each historical version dated correctly.
questions.additional_outcome_test: Application bunching near a verified age cutoff could be studied with complete submission records; current wording cannot establish strategic timing.

questions.question: Are short written review clocks attached to demanding eligibility requirements?
questions.economic_idea: A short formal deadline may apply only after the applicant clears costly documentation or validation steps. Comparing published targets alone can mis-rank entry requirements.
questions.test_with_existing_laws: Record clock start, calendar/working days, applicant stops, response rounds and eligibility alongside each target. Report comparable clocks separately from those that cannot be put on a common basis.
questions.additional_outcome_test: Separate pre-validation, active review and calendar elapsed time using receipt, validation, query and final-decision dates.

questions.question: Does reliance substitute for domestic scientific capacity, or require capacity to make use of it?
questions.economic_idea: Foreign review can save assessment resources, while report exchange, local adaptation and surveillance can require complementary expertise. The direction is an empirical question.
questions.test_with_existing_laws: Distinguish mandatory reliance, discretionary powers, scope of local review and report-sharing requirements. The law-only output describes these institutional combinations.
questions.additional_outcome_test: Interact verified reform eligibility with pre-reform assessor staffing/workload using case-level time and uptake outcomes; do not relabel national income or education as regulator capacity.
literature_template: Public Procurement in Law and Practice

questions.question: How long does legal permission take to become a route companies can actually use?
questions.economic_idea: Passing a rule, opening applications, receiving the first application and completing the first case are different events. Administrative implementation may be an economically important margin.
questions.test_with_existing_laws: Separate enacted permission, effective date, operational instructions, pilots, drafts and explicitly documented implementation. First found use is not necessarily first actual use.
questions.additional_outcome_test: Link original rule histories to first accepted and completed applications and annual pathway counts, with archive completeness checks.
literature_template: The World Price of Insider Trading
Public Procurement in Law and Practice

questions.question: Do countries borrow the same words while imposing different entry requirements?
questions.economic_idea: Template diffusion can make laws look harmonized even when eligibility, discretion or documentation differ. Textual convergence and functional convergence are distinct.
questions.test_with_existing_laws: Compare closest text matches with the fixed-case requirements matrix. Mask country/agency names, stratify by legal genre and translation basis, and account for shared regional templates.
questions.additional_outcome_test: Test whether functional differences predict practice only after operational data exist; text similarity alone does not establish institutional effectiveness.

questions.question: Does regulatory integration reach medicines equally when their manufacturers or factories change?
questions.economic_idea: An assessment may be reusable only for the same product, dossier, licensee or manufacturing process. Portability can therefore depend on the organization of production and rights, rather than the ingredient alone.
questions.test_with_existing_laws: Keep evidence and active ingredient constant while varying a manufacturing-site or authorized-licensee change where the rule expressly distinguishes it. Separate sameness checks from legal barriers to new entrants.
questions.additional_outcome_test: Link validated site/ownership changes to regulatory variations and actual entry costs. Do not infer market power from a sameness clause alone.

questions.question: Do foreign regulatory decisions travel more readily in the negative direction?
questions.economic_idea: A country may require additional work to accept an approval but react directly to a foreign suspension or safety withdrawal. This would make international information transmission asymmetric.
questions.test_with_existing_laws: Code foreign approval recognition separately from foreign rejection, withdrawal, suspension and notification clauses for the same medicine and references. Identify automatic, discretionary and evidence-only effects in each direction.
questions.additional_outcome_test: Measure actual transmission of safety actions with dated reference and destination decisions; distinguish regulator safety actions from manufacturers’ commercial withdrawals.
literature_template: The World Price of Insider Trading

questions.question: Does recognizing a medicine also open the market to additional suppliers?
questions.economic_idea: Approval portability for an originator does not automatically imply portability for generics, biosimilars or independent importers. Institutional integration may operate at a product–applicant level.
questions.test_with_existing_laws: Compare the fixed originator case with separately specified generic, biosimilar and authorized-import cases, retaining data rights, product identity and applicant requirements rather than pooling them.
questions.additional_outcome_test: Study supplier counts and price competition only with validated product/application types, launch/reimbursement records and dose/pack-matched prices.
